network.applySuccess: Candidate configuration applied. Please verify within window.
network.cancelSuccess: Rolled back to previous network configuration.
network.disconnectWarning: Changing IP or Primary Interface may temporarily interrupt your connection.
network.factoryResetConfirm: Are you sure you want to reset this interface to factory baseline?
network.guide1: 1. WAN (Primary): Used for internet & cloud uplink. Default gateway and system DNS can only be assigned to this port.
network.guide2: 2. LAN (Subnet/Direct): Ideal for RTSP camera/sensor subnets. Only assign IP & Subnet Mask; do NOT configure gateway to prevent routing conflicts.
network.guide3: 3. 120s Safe Protocol: Network changes enter a 120-second pending window. If connectivity is lost, settings auto-rollback.
network.modeDHCPDesc: Recommended. Upstream router dynamically assigns IP, subnet mask, and default gateway.
network.modeStaticDesc: For industrial isolated LAN or fixed IP deployment. Manually specify IP, mask, and routing.
network.pendingTip: Candidate configuration is active. If connection fails and not confirmed before countdown expires, settings will auto-rollback.
network.primarySwitchTip: Designate as the default gateway interface (handles 0.0.0.0/0 route and system DNS)
network.reconnectAlert: Gateway or IP changed. Reconnect using candidate addresses:
network.resetSuccess: Factory baseline restored and entered pending window.
network.topologyTip: Multi-Homing Isolation: Designate the upstream router port as Primary (WAN), and others as isolated LANs for RTSP cameras/sensors.
network.modeTip: Host-wide network mode and link failover
network.modeUnsupportedTip: Active-backup is not supported on this platform
network.modeEnterConfirm: Enable active-backup mode? The network topology will be rebuilt and this session may briefly disconnect. You must confirm within 120s.
network.modeExitConfirm: Exit active-backup mode? The bond will be removed and slaves returned.
network.modeSwitchWarning: Switching will rebuild the network topology and may briefly disconnect this session. Confirm within 120 seconds or it rolls back automatically.
network.modeSwitchSuccess: Mode switch submitted, confirm within the countdown
network.modeSlaveTip: Pick one active and one backup from writable physical interfaces
network.modeExitLACPConfirm: Exit LACP aggregation mode? The bond will be removed and slaves returned.
network.modeLACPNotice: Pre-requisite: Upstream switch must configure dynamic 802.3ad LAG. A single connection will not span physical links; inbound traffic distribution is determined by the switch hash.
network.modeLACPSlaveTip: Pick 2 or more writable physical interfaces for aggregation
network.modeXmitHashPolicyTip: Must align with switch hash policy, defaults to layer2+3
network.modeLACPDiagnosticPartnerNotConfigured: Diagnostic: No LACP response from partner switch, likely due to unconfigured 802.3ad LAG on upstream switch.
network.modeSlaveLinkMismatchWarning: Warning: Selected interface speed or duplex settings do not match; kernel may exclude some interfaces from aggregation.
network.modeExitGatewayConfirm: Exit edge gateway mode? Built-in DHCP server will stop, interface will be released, and ip_forward restored.
network.modeGatewayDownstreamTip: Select downstream dedicated LAN interface for cameras (must be static IPv4 and not WAN)
network.modeGatewayIPForwardDesc: Enabling ip_forward allows routing across subnets. Note: NAT is not performed; downstream cameras cannot initiate outbound internet access, and upstream hosts require reverse routes to reach cameras.
network.modeGatewayWarning: Enabling this will serve DHCP requests on the chosen interface broadcast domain. Ensure this interface is NOT connected to an external production network!
network.gatewayConflictWarning: Warning: Another active DHCP server was detected on this downstream interface link!

time.title: Time Management
time.modeNTPDesc: Recommended. Synchronizes continuously with network time servers, ensuring high accuracy and drift compensation.
time.modeManualDesc: Suitable for air-gapped or isolated networks. The system clock is set manually by an administrator.
time.serverListDesc: Tried in order of priority from top to bottom. Supports IPv4, IPv6, and domain names.
time.serverPlaceholder: Enter NTP server hostname or IP (e.g. pool.ntp.org)
time.confirmApplyManualTime: Setting system time manually will disable automatic NTP sync. Continue?
time.serverRequired: At least one valid NTP server is required in NTP mode
time.offsetTip: Offset between local clock and source
time.guide1: 1. Keeping NTP automatic sync active is recommended when the device has internet access to ensure precise video & event timestamps.
time.guide2: 2. In isolated LAN environments, you can configure local LAN NTP server addresses as preferred servers.
time.guide3: 3. Manual time changes should only be used when necessary. Events produced may carry time_synced=false.
